questions.question: Dr. Asma must restore a deep occlusal caries on a molar. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on mechanical properties, which material offers the best wear resistance for an occlusal restoration?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Nanohybrid composites offer excellent wear resistance for occlusal areas subjected to high stresses.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use a nanohybrid composite for this restoration.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must restore a non-carious cervical lesion on a premolar. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice of material. Based on adhesion properties, which material is most indicated?
options: Glass ionomer cement or a flowable composite with adhesive
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Cervical lesions require an adhesive material like GIC or a flowable composite with a good adhesive system.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use a GIC for its fluoride release.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must make an aesthetic veneer on an incisor. Dr. Kamal asks her which material offers the best aesthetic rendering. Based on optical properties, what is the material of choice?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Ceramics like lithium disilicate offer exceptional translucency and optical integration for veneers.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use lithium disilicate for this veneer.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must restore a deep caries on a primary tooth in a child. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice of material. Based on biological properties, which material is most indicated?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'GIC is ideal for primary teeth because it releases fluoride and chemically adheres to dentin.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use a GIC for this restoration.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must perform a posterior restoration on a molar with a Class II cavity. Dr. Kamal asks her how to manage the C-factor. According to the principles of adhesive dentistry, which technique reduces polymerization shrinkage?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Incremental layering reduces the C-factor and stresses related to polymerization shrinkage.' Dr. Asma: 'I will stratify my restoration in several layers.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must choose an adhesive system for a composite restoration. Dr. Asma asks him what the standard protocol for enamel adhesion is. According to the principles of adhesion, what is the standard concentration of phosphoric acid?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: '37% phosphoric acid is the standard for enamel etching.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use a 37% phosphoric acid gel.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must restore a deep cavity with pulpal proximity. Dr. Kamal advises her to use a liner. According to therapeutic properties, which material is indicated as a protective liner?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Calcium hydroxide and GICs have therapeutic and protective properties for the pulp.' Dr. Asma: 'I will place a calcium hydroxide liner.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must make an aesthetic restoration on an anterior tooth. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice of shade. According to the principles of dental aesthetics, when should the shade of the composite be chosen?
options: Before any preparation, under appropriate lighting
Only at the end of treatment
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'The shade should be chosen before preparation, under neutral lighting and after tooth hydration.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will choose the shade before starting the preparation.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must perform a composite restoration on a vital tooth. Dr. Kamal reminds her of the importance of pulpal protection. According to biological principles, what is the risk of an improperly polymerized composite?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Incomplete polymerization alters physical properties and can cause post-operative sensitivity.' Dr. Asma: 'I will ensure optimal polymerization.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must restore a cavity on a tooth with a difficult operative field. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice of material. Based on handling properties, which material is best suited in the presence of moisture?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'GIC is moisture-tolerant and chemically adheres to the tooth, making it suitable for difficult fields.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use a GIC.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must perform a restoration on a tooth with a Class V cavity. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on adhesion and fluoride release properties, which material is most indicated?
options: Glass ionomer cement or flowable composite with adhesive
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Cervical lesions benefit from the fluoride release of GIC or the adhesion of composite with an adhesive system.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use a resin-modified GIC.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must perform a direct restoration on a tooth with a deep cavity. Dr. Asma advises him to use the sandwich technique. According to the principles of adhesive dentistry, what does this technique consist of?
options: Applying several layers of composite of different shades
Using a GIC in the deep layer covered with composite
Using only a calcium hydroxide liner
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'The sandwich technique consists of placing a GIC in depth for its fluoride release, then covering it with composite for its resistance.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use this technique for this deep cavity.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must polish a composite restoration. Dr. Kamal asks her why polishing is important. According to clinical principles, what is the benefit of polishing?
options: Increase the volume of the restoration
Reduce plaque retention and improve aesthetics
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'A smooth surface reduces plaque accumulation and improves aesthetic integration.' Dr. Asma: 'I will carry out careful polishing.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must perform a restoration on a tooth with subgingival caries. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice of material. Based on clinical properties, which material is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Reinforced GIC is moisture-tolerant and can be used subgingivally.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will use a reinforced GIC for this restoration.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must perform a composite restoration on a tooth with a large cavity. Dr. Kamal advises her to use a high filler content composite. According to mechanical properties, what is the advantage of a high filler content?
options: Better wear resistance and reduced polymerization shrinkage
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Highly filled composites offer better wear resistance and reduced polymerization shrinkage.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use a high filler content composite.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must choose an adhesive system for a composite restoration. Dr. Asma asks him what the role of the coupling agent (silane) is. According to the principles of adhesion, what is the function of silane?
options: Modify the shade of the composite
Chemically bond the fillers to the resin matrix
Increase the fluidity of the material
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Silane ensures the bonding interface between the mineral filler and the organic resin.' Dr. Kamal: 'I better understand the role of silane.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must perform a restoration on a tooth with recurrent caries. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on biological properties, which material offers the best protection against recurrent caries?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'GIC releases fluoride, which helps prevent recurrent caries.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use a GIC for this restoration.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must perform a composite restoration on a tooth with a Class III cavity. Dr. Asma advises him on the operative technique. According to the principles of adhesive dentistry, what is the key step of enamel adhesion?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Etching with 37% phosphoric acid is the key step to creating micromechanical retention on enamel.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will perform the etching correctly.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must perform a restoration on a tooth with a Class IV cavity. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of material. Based on aesthetic and mechanical properties, which material is most indicated?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Nanohybrid composites offer an excellent aesthetic and mechanical compromise for Class IV restorations.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use a nanohybrid composite.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must perform a restoration on a tooth with deep caries. Dr. Asma advises him to use a base. According to the principles of restorative dentistry, what is the role of a base?
options: Protect the pulp and compensate for lost volume
Modify the shade of the restoration
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'A base protects the pulp and fills the lost volume before placing the definitive restoration.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will place a base before the composite.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must perform a composite restoration on a tooth with a Class I cavity. Dr. Kamal asks her how to manage the C-factor. According to clinical principles, what is the C-factor of a Class I cavity?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Class I cavities have a high C-factor, meaning there are more bonded than free surfaces.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use layering to manage this C-factor.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must choose a light curing lamp for his practice. Dr. Asma asks him what the optimal wavelength for composite photopolymerization is. According to physical principles, what is this wavelength?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Blue light (440-480 nm) is necessary to activate the composite photoinitiator.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will choose a lamp with this wavelength.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma must perform a composite restoration on a tooth with a Class V cavity. Dr. Kamal advises her on the choice of adhesive system. According to the principles of adhesion, which type of adhesive is recommended for dentin?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Total-etch adhesives are recommended for optimal adhesion to dentin and enamel.' Dr. Asma: 'I will use a total-etch adhesive.'

questions.question: Dr. Kamal must perform a restoration on a tooth with sub-occlusal caries. Dr. Asma advises him on the choice of material. Based on mechanical properties, which material offers the best compressive strength?
questions.explanation: Dr. Asma explains: 'Amalgam offers excellent compressive strength, although it is less aesthetic.' Dr. Kamal: 'I will consider amalgam for this occlusal area.'

questions.question: Dr. Asma, after having performed several restorations with Dr. Kamal, receives his congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. Asma?
options: Become an expert in dental materials
questions.explanation: Dr. Kamal explains: 'Mastery of dental materials is a valuable skill. Becoming an expert is the next step.' Dr. Asma: 'I will train in new materials.'
